function: Per-AP antenna selection (CNN classifier) and precoding design (GNN) maximizing downlink sum spectral efficiency of a cell-free MIMO network from local estimated CSI (p. 1-4).
system: Downlink cell-free MIMO, TDD block fading: I=3 APs, N=8 antennas (M=5 active), K=4 single-antenna users, 20 MHz bandwidth, carrier not stated, LMMSE CSI; no RIS (p. 2-3, 8).
method: GNN precoder per AP, unsupervised with negative sum-SE loss; CNN antenna classifier, supervised cross-entropy on labels from iterative search; both trained offline at the CPU (p. 5-8).
data_channel: Simulated Rayleigh block fading, path loss exponent 3.67; users uniform in 300x300 m; 2x10^4 CNN training samples per AP; GNN trained on random user locations (p. 3, 8-10).
test_conditions: Default K=4, I=3, N=8, M=5, 20 dBm; sweeps over K, Pmax, M, N, I, pilot length (Figs. 14-19); retraining per setting not stated (p. 8, 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: centralized MMSE + iterative search, centralized MMSE, distributed MMSE, MRT; learned: MLP and CNN precoders, GNN and MLP antenna selectors (Figs. 11, 13-19, p. 9-12).
metrics: Sum spectral efficiency (bit/s/Hz), computation time in ms, information exchange in complex scalars (Table II, p. 10-13).
complexity: Orders of complexity for CNN and GNN layers, and for MMSE schemes (p. 12); Table II: 0.76 ms versus 227.6 ms for centralized MMSE + IS (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 3: "The small-scale fading is assumed to follow Rayleigh distribution." p. 8: "α = 3.67 represents the path loss exponent [40]"; a custom simulator with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 8: "The default simulation parameters are summarized in Table I unless otherwise stated." Figs. 14-19 sweep K, Pmax, M, N, I and pilot length, but the paper never states that a model trained at one setting is tested at another.
q3_support: p. 9: "MLP-based baseline algorithms to perform the precoding design as comparisons to the proposed GNN-based algorithm"; p. 10: "the proposed GNN + CNN scheme significantly outperforms the distributed benchmark schemes" (MMSE, MRT).
q4_support: p. 12: "The total computational complexity is the sum of the above complexity." p. 13: "the proposed GNN + CNN scheme achieves 95.6% sum spectral efficiency with only 0.33% computational time."
q5_support: p. 8: "The users are uniformly and randomly distributed within a square area on the xy-plane"; the data are simulated by the authors, and no code or data link or availability statement appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: Included, area 3: the GNN designs the AP precoders and the CNN adds antenna selection, so the joint work stays physical layer. q2=0 because the paper does not say whether models are retrained or reused across the sweeps of Figs. 14-19; the CNN input is 2N x K and its output has C(N,M) units (p. 7), which suggests retraining, but this is my inference and is not stated. q3 uses non-learned MMSE and MRT baselines and standard CNN and MLP learned baselines on the same task. Tables I-II were read from the page images (pages 8, 13). Title and DOI 10.1109/TVT.2025.3590425 are on page 1.
